markets: Trades physical commodities worldwide from Geneva, with offices across Europe, the Americas and Asia.
rationale: Private trader with low consumer visibility; F1 value would mainly be B2B hospitality with energy and shipping partners.

name: NextDecade
desc: Houston developer building the Rio Grande LNG export facility in Brownsville, Texas, with five planned trains.
markets: Single US Gulf Coast project selling LNG under long-term contracts to international energy companies; not yet in operation.
rationale: Single-project LNG developer with no consumer brand; F1 would only offer B2B hospitality to offtake partners.

name: NRG Energy
desc: US power company generating and retailing electricity and natural gas to millions of homes and businesses under brands like Reliant.
markets: Retail and generation customers across the United States; no wider international footprint known.
rationale: Consumer-facing US energy retailer with strong brands, but US-only reach limits international F1 value.

name: Pattern Energy Group
desc: Developer and owner of wind, solar, transmission and storage projects, including the SunZia Wind and Transmission project in New Mexico.
markets: Projects in the United States, Canada, Mexico and Japan selling power to utilities and corporate buyers.
rationale: B2B renewable developer with no consumer brand; sustainability messaging possible but limited marketing culture.
changed: Acquired by CPP Investments in 2020

name: ReNew
desc: Indian independent power producer of wind, solar, hydro and storage capacity, selling power to government agencies and corporates.
markets: Operations and customers in India; no verified overseas expansion.
rationale: Indian renewable producer with large scale but B2B customers; India F1 interest is emerging.

name: Sonnedix
desc: Independent solar power producer owning and operating solar plants across Europe, the United States, Chile, Japan and South Africa.
markets: Plants across Europe, the Americas, Japan and South Africa, selling power to utilities and corporate buyers.
rationale: Infrastructure-owned solar producer with no consumer brand; a sustainability partnership could suit F1 but marketing scale is small.

name: Sysco
desc: Foodservice distributor delivering food, kitchen supplies and equipment to restaurants, hospitals, hotels and schools.
markets: Serves customers in the United States, Canada, Europe and Latin America.
rationale: Largest foodservice distributor with hospitality customers worldwide; F1 could showcase catering supply, but brand marketing is B2B.

name: Talen Energy
desc: Independent power producer owning nuclear, natural gas and other power plants in US PJM and ERCOT markets.
markets: Sells power in US markets and supplies data centres such as Amazon's campus; no international operations.
rationale: US-only wholesale power producer with little consumer marketing; F1 fit is weak beyond data-centre power positioning.

name: TenneT
desc: Electricity transmission system operator running the high-voltage grid in the Netherlands and a large part of Germany.
markets: Grids in the Netherlands and Germany, with offshore grid connections for North Sea wind farms.
rationale: Regulated state-owned grid operator with no consumer brand; F1 fit is weak.
changed: Sold a minority stake in TenneT Germany to investors in 2025

name: TenneT Germany
desc: German arm of TenneT operating high-voltage transmission lines from Schleswig-Holstein to Bavaria and connecting offshore wind farms.
markets: Transmission grid in Germany, including North Sea offshore wind connections.
rationale: Regulated German grid operator with no consumer brand and little marketing culture; F1 fit is weak.
changed: Minority stake sold to investors in 2025

name: Trafigura
desc: Commodity trader of crude oil, refined products, metals, minerals, gas, power and agricultural goods, operating from Singapore and Geneva.
markets: Trades commodities worldwide from Singapore and Geneva, with fuel retail and terminals in many countries.
rationale: Private trader with low consumer visibility; F1 value would be B2B hospitality and brand building with energy and shipping partners.

name: Uniper
desc: German energy company trading and generating power and gas, operating gas storage and LNG and supplying industrial customers in Europe.
industry: power and gas trading and generation
markets: Operations and customers mainly across Europe, with LNG and trading activities.
rationale: Nationalised energy firm with mostly B2B customers; state ownership and restructuring make F1 sponsorship unlikely.
changed: Rescued and nationalised by the German state in 2022

name: Vistra
desc: Integrated power company generating electricity from gas, nuclear, coal, solar and storage and retailing power under brands including TXU Energy.
markets: Retail and generation customers across the United States; no international operations known.
rationale: US power retailer with consumer brands and Texas presence, where the US Grand Prix is held, though reach is domestic.

name: Williams
desc: Energy infrastructure company owning the Transco natural gas pipeline and gathering and processing assets across the United States.
markets: Fee-based gas transport and processing for producers and utilities in the United States.
rationale: Regulated-style US pipeline operator with no consumer brand; F1 would offer only B2B hospitality.

name: ACME Solar
desc: Indian renewable energy developer and independent power producer owning solar, wind and hybrid projects.
markets: Projects and customers in India; no verified overseas operations.
rationale: Indian renewable producer with B2B customers and no consumer brand; F1 fit is weak.
changed: Listed on Indian exchanges after a 2024 IPO

name: Adani Green Energy
desc: Indian renewable energy company in the Adani Group with solar, wind and hybrid projects, including the Khavda park in Gujarat.
markets: Projects and customers in India, selling power to government agencies and utilities.
rationale: Large Indian renewable producer in a conglomerate with brand ambitions; India's F1 interest could suit, but customers are B2B.

name: AES
desc: Global power company generating and distributing electricity, including renewables and storage, through utilities in the US and other countries.
markets: Utilities in the United States and operations in Chile, Brazil and other countries.
rationale: Large power company with a utility brand, but customers are mostly B2B or regulated; F1 fit is moderate at best.

name: Alabama Power Company
desc: Regulated electric utility serving about 1.5 million customers across most of Alabama, with nuclear, coal, gas and hydro generation.
markets: Customers across Alabama only; a subsidiary of Southern Company.
rationale: Regulated state utility with a local customer base; F1 sponsorship would not fit its mandate.

name: American Electric Power
desc: US utility owning the nation's largest electricity transmission network, with generation and distribution utilities in 11 states.
markets: Customers in 11 US states; no international operations.
rationale: Regulated US utility with limited marketing culture; F1 fit is weak beyond B2B hospitality.

name: Arevon
desc: Developer, owner and operator of utility-scale solar and battery storage projects across the United States.
markets: US utility-scale projects selling power to utilities and corporate buyers.
rationale: B2B renewable developer with no consumer brand; sustainability partnership possible but limited marketing scale.

name: Atlas Renewable Energy
desc: Renewable energy company developing and operating solar projects, mainly in Latin America, selling power to utilities and corporate buyers.
markets: Projects in Brazil, Chile, Colombia, Mexico and Peru, selling to utilities and corporate buyers.
rationale: Latin American solar developer with B2B customers; Brazil and Mexico races give regional relevance but brand scale is small.

name: Avaada
desc: Indian green energy company developing solar, wind, battery storage and green hydrogen, supplying power to utilities and corporates.
markets: Projects and customers in India; no verified overseas operations.
rationale: Indian renewable developer with B2B customers and limited consumer brand; F1 fit is weak.

name: Avantus
desc: Developer of large-scale solar and solar-plus-storage projects across the western US, formerly 8minute Solar Energy.
markets: Western US projects selling power to utilities and corporate buyers.
rationale: B2B solar developer with no consumer brand and limited marketing culture; F1 fit is weak.
changed: Renamed from 8minute Solar Energy to Avantus in 2021

name: Aypa Power
desc: Developer and owner of large-scale battery storage and renewable energy projects in the United States, backed by Blackstone.
markets: US storage and renewable projects serving utilities and grid operators.
rationale: B2B storage developer with no consumer brand and limited marketing culture; F1 fit is weak.

name: Clean Power Alliance
desc: Public community choice aggregator buying and supplying cleaner electricity to customer accounts in Los Angeles and Ventura counties.
markets: Serves Los Angeles and Ventura County customers in California only.
rationale: Local public electricity agency; sponsorship by a government body is very unlikely.

name: Comision Federal de Electricidad (CFE)
desc: Mexico's state-owned electric utility generating, transmitting and distributing power to around 48 million customers.
markets: Customers across Mexico only; no international operations known, though the Mexico City Grand Prix is local.
rationale: State utility with Mexican reach; Mexico City Grand Prix visibility is possible but state-owned procurement limits sponsorship.
